title: DevOps & Cloud Engineering Readiness
description: Assess your expertise in Linux commands, Docker containers, Kubernetes clusters, CI/CD pipelines, Terraform, and cloud reliability.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between a Docker container and a Virtual Machine (VM)?
options: Containers share the host operating system kernel and are lightweight; VMs run a full guest OS on a hypervisor
VMs do not require an operating system
Containers only run on Linux
Containers cannot run microservices
questions.explanation: Containers isolate processes using Linux namespaces and cgroups sharing the host kernel, whereas VMs virtualize hardware and run independent guest OS kernels.

questions.question: In Kubernetes, what is the smallest deployable computing unit that can be created and managed?
options: Pod
Container
Service
Node
questions.explanation: A Pod encapsulates one or more co-located containers, shared storage volumes, and a unique network IP.

questions.question: What is Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and what problem does it solve?
options: Managing and provisioning computing infrastructure through version-controlled declarative code files, eliminating manual configuration drift
Writing Python scripts directly inside AWS EC2 instances
Encrypting database tables automatically
Monitoring server RAM and CPU metrics
questions.explanation: IaC tools like Terraform enable reproducible, automated, and version-controlled infrastructure definitions across cloud providers.

questions.question: What command in Terraform compares the desired configuration state with the actual infrastructure state and creates an execution plan?
options: terraform plan
terraform apply
terraform init
terraform refresh
questions.explanation: `terraform plan` creates an execution plan, previewing the resources Terraform will create, update, or destroy before applying.

questions.question: In CI/CD, what is the core difference between Continuous Delivery and Continuous Deployment?
options: Continuous Delivery requires manual approval before releasing to production; Continuous Deployment automatically releases every passed build to production
Continuous Delivery only compiles code without testing
Continuous Deployment only works with Docker
There is no difference between them
questions.explanation: Continuous Delivery keeps code in an always-deployable state with manual sign-off; Continuous Deployment automates release straight to production.

questions.question: In Linux file permissions, what does the numeric permission `chmod 755 filename` grant?
options: Owner: Read/Write/Execute (7); Group: Read/Execute (5); Others: Read/Execute (5)
Owner: Read only; Everyone else: Full access
Full read/write/execute permissions for everyone
Restricted read-only access for all users
questions.explanation: 7 (4+2+1 = rwx) for owner, 5 (4+0+1 = r-x) for group, and 5 (4+0+1 = r-x) for others.

questions.question: In AWS networking, what is the role of a NAT Gateway in a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)?
options: Enables instances in a private subnet to initiate outbound internet traffic while preventing inbound internet connections
Distributes incoming user traffic across multiple EC2 instances
Stores relational database backups
Resolves internal DNS domain names
questions.explanation: NAT Gateways allow backend private resources (like database servers or worker instances) to download software updates from the web without exposing them to incoming attacks.

questions.question: What is a 'Blue-Green Deployment' strategy?
options: Maintaining two identical production environments; new code is deployed to the idle (Green) environment and router traffic is switched instantly once verified
Deploying changes to 10% of users randomly
Shutting down all servers for maintenance during midnight
Deploying frontend and backend simultaneously
questions.explanation: Blue-Green deployment eliminates downtime and reduces deployment risk by running two identical environments and swapping traffic instantly.

questions.question: In Prometheus monitoring, what is the difference between a Counter and a Gauge metric?
options: A Counter only increases (or resets to 0 on restart); a Gauge is a value that can go up and down (like memory usage)
A Gauge only counts integer increments
Counters are stored in databases; Gauges are discarded
A Gauge measures HTTP status codes exclusively
questions.explanation: Counters represent cumulative metrics that only rise (e.g. total HTTP requests), whereas Gauges represent instantaneous snapshots (e.g. current memory utilization).

questions.question: What does a Multi-Stage Dockerfile achieve?
options: Separates the heavy build environment from the lean runtime container, resulting in tiny, secure production images
Runs multiple operating systems in a single container
Automatically scales containers across regions
Deploys images to AWS and GCP simultaneously
questions.explanation: Multi-stage builds leave compilers, SDKs, and build dependencies in temporary stages, copying only the compiled artifacts into the final production image.
